title: Turn-Based Stochastic Mean-Payoff Games in Deterministic Quasipolynomial Time
main_claim: Theorem 1.1: a uniform deterministic algorithm outputs exactly U={i : val(i) >= 0} for finite turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games (expected pathwise liminf payoff, binary-encoded integer rewards and rational probabilities) using 2^{O(log^2(L+2))} bit operations.
coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX sources (introduction, discount, labeling and application sections) and checked every step of the main proof by hand.

Section 2, the discount reduction:
- Entry norms of Q(I-(1-u)P) are at most 2Q (the paper uses 3Q). The coefficient norms of D and N_i are at most A0, and the edge-comparison numerator is at most (3+W)A0 <= H.
- Sign stabilization holds for 0 < u <= 1/(2H). A comparison that vanishes at lambda0 vanishes identically. Since lambda0 = 1/(32H^2) <= 1/(2H), the positional pair stays optimal on the whole interval.
- The gain G = N̂(0)/D̂(0) has denominator at most A0, which gives the value gap 1/H. The error bound is |v - G| <= 2(1+W)A0·u <= 2Hu = 1/(16H) at u = lambda0.
- The gain/bias identities and inequalities at player and chance vertices follow correctly from the expansion.
- Lemma 2.2 (finite-valued submartingale) and Lemma 2.3 (bounded martingale differences, Chebyshev along squares) both hold.
- The pathwise argument holds for both players against behavioral opponents, including the liminf/limsup handling.

Section 3, the labeling:
- Comparison principle and the finite box iteration hold.
- Mechanics: integrality when d >= 12, nesting of child boxes, and at most 1024n+1 calls per pass.
- The rank d+B decreases at every child, and the mass products grow by 4/3 >= 32/25 in the passes and by exactly 32/25 in the continuation.
- Translation lemma: the peak is at least 11D/32 and the gap outside the support is at least 23D/32 > D/2. The sign of t is right: t < 0 for subsolutions and t > 0 for supersolutions, so gamma·t >= t and gamma·t <= t respectively.
- Downward and upward passes: the peak stays constant (moving coordinates have gap > p >= delta), override exclusions use 7D/16 > 3D/8, the cap arguments hold, and the downward mass bound carries through the upward pass because gaps are nonincreasing.
- Reweighting: (8/5) - (4/5)(3/4) = 1. The override priority logic is correct, and both base cases are correct.

Section 4, the application:
- F(t) = S·f_lambda(t/S) has gamma = 1 - 1/N. The vectors Y and Z are a sub- and supersolution since gamma(N+1) = N - 1/N.
- The gap is at most K/128 < D/128, and each box shrink step is safe since 3D/128 >= delta.
- Final error is 1/(16H) + 1/(16H) = 1/(8H), and the threshold -1/(2H), i.e. A_i >= -8K, is correct.
- Tree-size count is (Lambda+1)(B0+1)(1+Lambda·s*)^{B0} with B0 = O(log n) and Lambda = O(L^2), which gives the claimed quasipolynomial bound. Bit lengths are polynomial, with common denominator QN.

I did not run a numerical implementation of the procedure. Recursion at d >= 12 is impractical, and a sibling branch already validated the deterministic analogue empirically.
sibling_notes: This paper extends the companion Deterministic-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games paper (Sections 4–5, two-pass pivot labeling) to discounted operators. The labeling theorem is reproved in full here, and the discount reduction is self-contained, so nothing depends circularly on companion lemmas. The sibling review found that companion clean, and its structure matches what I checked here.
